title: Recommandations de Tokyo (Tokyo Guidelines) 2018 pour la cholangite aiguë
short_title: Recommandations de Tokyo sur les angiocholites
formula:
Patient must have a suspected diagnosis (≥1 item in A + ≥1 item in B or C) or definite diagnosis (≥1 item in A, B, and C) to meet entry criteria for severity grading, see table below:

**Diagnosis:**

| Criteria | |
| --- | --- |
| Part A | |
| Systemic inflammation | Fever >38°C (100.4°F) and/or shaking chills |
| Laboratory data: evidence of inflammatory response WBC <4,000 /mm³ or >10,000 /mm³ (<4 × 10⁹ /L or >10 × 10⁹ /L) and/or CRP ≥1 mg/dL (10 mg/L) | |
| Part B | |
| Cholestasis | Jaundice Total bilirubin ≥2 mg/dL (34.2 μmol/L) |
| Laboratory data: abnormal liver enzymes ALP, γGTP, AST, ALT levels >1.5 × upper limit of normal | |
| Part C | |
| Imaging | Biliary dilatation |
| Evidence of the etiology on imaging (stricture, stone, stent, etc.) | |

**Severity grading:**

| Grade III (dysfunction in ≥1 of the following): |
| --- |
| Cardiovascular dysfunction: hypotension requiring dopamine ≥5 μg/kg per min or any dose of norepinephrine |
| Neurological dysfunction: disturbance of consciousness |
| Respiratory dysfunction: PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio <300 |
| Renal dysfunction: oliguria or creatinine >2.0 mg/dL (176.8 μmol/L) |
| Hepatic dysfunction: PT‐INR >1.5 |
| Hematological dysfunction: platelet count <100,000 /mm³ (<100 × 10⁹ /L) |
| Grade II (≥2 of the following conditions): |
| Abnormal WBC count >12,000 /mm³ or <4,000 /mm³ (>12 × 10⁹ /L or <4 × 10⁹ /L) |
| High fever ≥39°C (102.2°F) |
| Age ≥75 years |
| Hyperbilirubinemia Total bilirubin ≥5 mg/dL (85.5 μmol/L) |
| Hypoalbuminemia <0.7 × lower limit of normal |
| Grade I |
| Does not meet the criteria of Grade III or Grade II acute cholangitis at initial diagnosis |

how_to_use.why:
- Guide de façon objective le diagnostic et la prise en charge des patients atteints d’angiocholite aiguë en termes de moment et de nécessité d’un drainage biliaire et de soins de support.
- La triade de Charcot (fièvre, douleur de l’hypochondre droit, ictère) a une spécificité élevée mais une sensibilité faible pour l’angiocholite aiguë ([Kiriyama et al 2017](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jhbp.512)).
how_to_use.when: À utiliser chez les patients présentant une suspicion d’angiocholite aiguë (c.-à-d. fièvre, ictère, douleur de l’hypochondre droit, altération de l’état mental et/ou instabilité hémodynamique).
how_to_use.pearls:
- More extensively studied in non-US populations.
- Conditions such as acute hepatitis and acute cholecystitis may have some similarities in presentation and should be ruled out.
- Although MRI andMRCPhave the highest sensitivity/specificity for bile duct dilation, abdominal US followed by CT abdomen are more readily available and cost-effective, and thus should be performed initially.
- Procalcitonin is useful in assessing the severity of cholangitis, *not* in the diagnosis.
- For patients with grade II-III (moderate to severe) cholangitis, transfer to a hospital that can perform biliary drainage and provide ICU level care is recommended.

next_steps.advice:
- Si un diagnostic définitif ne peut être posé lors de la présentation initiale, il est raisonnable de réévaluer le patient à l’aide des critères diagnostiques toutes les 6 à 12 h.
- Chez les patients présentant une maladie de grade I (légère), si aucune réponse au traitement initial n’est observée dans les 24 h, réaliser immédiatement un drainage biliaire.
- Chez les patients présentant une maladie de grade II (modérée) ou de grade III (sévère), réaliser un drainage biliaire dès que possible avec des soins de support et des antibiotiques. De plus, obtenir des hémocultures et des cultures biliaires chez ces patients.
- Envisager de traiter l’étiologie de l’angiocholite aiguë par une intervention endoscopique (sphinctérotomie endoscopique ou cholédocolithotomie), percutanée ou chirurgicale une fois la maladie aiguë résolue. La cholécystectomie doit être réalisée en cas de lithiase biliaire après résolution de l’angiocholite aiguë.
- Les antibiotiques doivent être choisis en fonction de la gravité de la maladie, du site de l’infection (communautaire ou nosocomiale) et des sensibilités locales (voir [Tokyo Guidelines 2018 Antimicrobial Therapy for Acute Cholangitis and Cholecystitis](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/29090866)).
next_steps.management:
- Upon diagnosis of acute cholangitis (regardless of severity) initial treatment generally consists of antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, electrolyte repletion, and appropriate analgesic administration.

evidence:
- The[Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jhbp.509)are a revision of the[2013 guidelines (TG13)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23307001), and incorporate new evidence based on validation studies of TG13.
- [Kiriyama et al (2017)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jhbp.458)studied 6,063 patients who were clinically diagnosed with acute cholangitis, and found that the TG13 guidelines diagnosed 90% of these patients retrospectively with acute cholangitis. 30-day mortality rates of patients with Grade III, Grade II, and Grade I were 5.1%, 2.6%, and 1.2%, respectively, and increased significantly along with disease severity.
more_info:
Interpretation:

| Grade | Acute cholangitis severity | Recommendations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I | Mild | Antibiotics and general supportive care; consider biliary drainage if no response to initial treatment |
| II | Moderate | Antibiotics and general supportive care; early endoscopic or percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage is indicated |
| III | Severe | Initial treatment with antibiotics, urgent biliary drainage, appropriate respiratory/circulatory management |
